headline: Cell division builds complexity—one cell becomes trillions through repeated doubling
universal_truth: Small things compound; repeated doubling creates massive results from tiny beginnings
fun_facts: You started as one cell—that cell divided into the 37 trillion cells that make you now
Cell division is so fast that you produce about 300 billion new cells daily
After just 50 doublings, one cell could theoretically become more than all atoms in the observable universe
discussion_questions: What small thing in your life compounds over time?
Where could consistent doubling create massive results?
What started small but grew enormous?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: You were once a single cell. That cell divided into two. Two became four. Four became eight. After about 50 doublings, you became 37 trillion cells—heart, brain, skin, bones. From one to trillions through repeated division.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Growth through doubling seems slow at first but becomes explosive. What does this exponential pattern teach us?

options.text: Doubling is exponential—each step multiplies the total, so early stages seem slow but later stages explode; patience in early doublings yields massive late results
options.response: Yes. The first few doublings don't look impressive: 1, 2, 4, 8. But by doubling 50: over a quadrillion. Compound growth is deceptively powerful.

options.text: Having lots of cells just means having more material
options.response: True, but the pattern of growth—exponential rather than linear—is the key insight...

q1.title: Exponential Growth
q1.script: Linear growth adds: 1, 2, 3, 4... Exponential growth multiplies: 1, 2, 4, 8... After 50 steps, linear gives 50. Exponential gives over a quadrillion. The pattern difference is enormous.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Exponential Growth"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Early Patience
q2.script: Exponential curves look flat early on. The jump from 1 to 2 isn't impressive. But each doubling matters—it sets up the next. Patience in early stages is rewarded explosively later.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Compound Effects
q3.script: Money compounds. Skills compound. Relationships compound. Knowledge compounds. Anything that builds on itself can grow exponentially. Small consistent investments become enormous given time.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Small things compound. Repeated doubling creates massive results from tiny beginnings. Be patient with early stages—exponential growth is coming.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 246. Tomorrow, we'll explore how bodies fix themselves—healing. Until then, identify something in your life that's compounding.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Compound Identification - What's Growing Exponentially?
growTrack.activity: What in your life compounds—skills, relationships, savings, knowledge? Are you being patient with early stages? Small consistent investments in compounding areas yield enormous long-term results. Identify your doublings.
